related_questions.question: What is the life expectancy of a person with breast cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: Life expectancy with breast cancer varies significantly based on several factors, most notably the stage of the cancer at diagnosis. Early-stage breast cancer, where the cancer is localized to the breast, has a very high five-year survival rate, often exceeding 99%. However, survival rates decrease with more advanced stages, with distant or metastatic breast cancer having significantly lower five-year survival rates.
snippet_highlighted_words: Early-stage breast cancer, where the cancer is localized to the breast, has a very high five-year survival rate, often exceeding 99%

list.title: Localized Breast Cancer (Stage I):
list.snippet: Five-year survival rates are very high, often exceeding 99%, according to the American Cancer Society. This means that most women diagnosed with localized breast cancer will live for at least five years after diagnosis.

list.title: Regional Breast Cancer (Stage II & III):
list.snippet: The five-year survival rate for regional breast cancer, where the cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes, is around 87%.

list.title: Distant/Metastatic Breast Cancer (Stage IV):
list.snippet: When breast cancer has spread to distant parts of the body, the five-year survival rate drops to around 32%, according to the National Breast Cancer Foundation. It's important to note that this is a relative survival rate, meaning it compares the survival of people with breast cancer to the general population.

list.title: Overall Survival:
list.snippet: When all stages of breast cancer are combined, the five-year survival rate is around 91%, according to the National Breast Cancer Foundation.

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: Younger women may have different survival rates compared to older women, partly due to differences in tumor biology and screening practices.

list.title: Race and Ethnicity:
list.snippet: Survival rates can vary across different racial and ethnic groups.

list.title: Overall Health:
list.snippet: A person's overall health and any other existing medical conditions can also influence their prognosis.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: The type of treatment received, including surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, and targeted therapies, plays a crucial role in survival.

list.title: Molecular Subtype:
list.snippet: Different subtypes of breast cancer (e.g., hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive) respond differently to treatment and have varying prognoses.

list.title: Remission:
list.snippet: While stage IV breast cancer is not typically considered curable, some individuals can achieve long-term remission, where the cancer is undetectable and does not progress.
